newsitem.title: UK: BA says to unveil new livery "soon".
newsitem.headline: BA says to unveil new livery "soon".

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday that it will unveil a new livery and corporate identity this summer.
Chief executive Robert Ayling told the annual convention of the Institute of Directors that BA was reshaping itself to improve customer service.
"Our greater commitment to customers will soon be symbolised by a new livery," he said. "Watch this space. I promise something new and different."
"It will be in the summer," a company spokeswoman said after the speech.

"We are moving to a new livery which will reflect the global reach of the company. It is going to be very different and very exciting and reflecting the global nature of the company...Our customers want us to look more modern and more cosmopolitan."
She said the change would retain the British Airways brand and was not linked to BA's ambitions to form a major marketing alliance with American Airlines.
The company said that several rival airlines now had liveries which were at best similar to BA's grey and dark blue colours.
"It will help us differentiate again," the spokeswoman said.

She declined to detail the new livery, but to save costs on repainting when the new colours are introduced 40 aircraft were recently painted in an "interim livery" of pearl white with a lighter blue underbelly.

Ayling told the IOD that his industry was moving from "a sky packed full of national airlines to one with a smaller number of global competitors, with a fringe of low-cost operators where the business looks good."

In addition to alliances, BA was in the throes of undertaking a "step-change" programme which aimed to find annual cost savings of a billion pounds by the year 2000 and to realign its workforce to put a greater emphasis on customer service.

"Our customers have told us that they want more people at the service end of the business," Ayling said. "So we are investing in our workforce, the right workforce, with the right skills in the right roles to keep our customers coming back."
